cards.title: Don't leave the room confused
cards.body: Once you're out, the queue moves and the doctor is busy. A few questions before you stand up save three anxious phone calls later.

cards.title: What is each medicine for?
cards.body: Ask for every new one. Knowing that one tablet is for BP and another is for acidity helps everyone at home keep track.

cards.title: How and when exactly to take it?
cards.body: Before or after food? Morning or night? What does 1-0-1 mean for this one? Get the doctor to say it, and write it down right there.

cards.title: What if a dose gets missed?
cards.body: Every medicine is different. Ask the doctor or pharmacist what to do, so nobody at home guesses or doubles up out of panic.

cards.title: Which side effects should we watch?
cards.body: Which ones are common and harmless, and which mean you should call? Knowing the difference saves a lot of midnight worry.

cards.title: When do we come back, and why?
cards.body: Ask what the follow-up is for. Fresh tests? Readings to bring? A check on how the new medicine is working?

cards.title: When should we not wait?
cards.body: Ask which signs need urgent care. In general, chest pain, sudden weakness on one side, confusion, trouble breathing or fainting mean call 112 right away.

takeaway: Before you stand up, ask what each medicine is for, how to take it, what to watch for and when to return.
share: Questions to ask before leaving the doctor's room. Save this for Papa's next visit.
